$comment: The one motion duration scale of cmux NEXT (Leo 2026-10-20: "animations all around are a bit slow"). Every timed fade and every structural move ends within one of these steps; anything entering eases out, and a selection that travels may ride the one spring, and a fold that grows or shrinks settles on the settle curve (the spring a CSS linear() easing; the native side keeps its own spring physics, so the Swift copy has no spring). scripts/cmux-next/gen-motion-scale.py writes the Swift (MotionScale.generated.swift), CSS (--cmux-motion-<step> in webviews/src/pages/shared/desktop.css) and TypeScript (webviews/src/motion/scale.generated.ts) copies. Loops (spinners, breathing) and hover-intent delays are not transitions and stay off the scale; the one exception is `spinner`, the period every spinner turns at, which it also writes as --cmux-spinner-period (CSS), SPINNER_PERIOD_MS (TypeScript), MotionScale.spinnerPeriod (Swift) and design-tokens.json motion.loops.spinner (Rust).

steps.name: quick
steps.for: hover and pressed fills, focus rings, anything leaving (a popup, a notice, a row)

steps.name: micro
steps.for: small things arriving: a fade in, a popup opening, a chip, a tooltip

steps.name: standard
steps.for: structural changes: a row or card moving, a fold opening, a scrim

steps.name: large
steps.for: the largest moves, and the ceiling: a split, a zoom, a window closing, the launch mark

spinner.for: one turn of every spinner, app and pages alike: a calm turn, the reference spinner's (Leo 2026-11-07: "Let's have all our spinners go at that speed.")

send.for: a prompt the reader sends: its room opens, the bubble comes in from the right and the thread rises, in one motion that settles (Leo 2026-11-07: "it's all just one unified motion"); scaled with the move step by ui.animationSpeed

spring.for: a selection or view that travels to where it lands and settles with a touch of give (a sliding tab indicator, the chat switch); run over its step (large, 240 ms) it is visibly settled by 58% (about 140 ms) and at rest by the end

settle.for: a fold, a Show more or a panel that grows or shrinks to its new height: a strong ease-out that starts at full speed and decelerates into its end on a long soft tail, never past it (Leo 2026-11-07: "they dont overshoot but they decelerate at the end. i think that might be the key"). Measured on the reference panel's folds (split-motion-sweep, 4 events): a first-order exponential, 1 - e^(-t/38 ms), about 53% of the way in the first frame and within 0.5 pt of rest by about 225 ms, fold and unfold alike; this cubic-bezier over 265 ms is within 1.1% of it at every point. The exact curve as linear(0, .393, .632, .778, .866, .920, .952, .972, .984, .991, .996, .998, 1) over 230 ms is not the value because WebKit before Safari 17.2 (macOS 14.0 and 14.1) has no linear() easing. Native: the same CAMediaTimingFunction(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) over 0.265 s, or, where a spring must take an interruption, an overdamped one with mass 1, stiffness 20800 and damping 826
